The Rosario Islands lie off Cartagena in the Caribbean Sea. Here, city sightseeing gives way to beaches and seascapes. The coastal waters support coral ecosystems inhabited by tropical fish, sponges and other marine organisms. A boat trip offers views of the islands from the water.

A stay in the archipelago centers on the chosen island and its shoreline. Beyond the beach, visitors can enjoy diving and boat trips; some routes include kayaking through mangroves. A few days by the sea in the Rosario Islands often round out a journey through Colombia, with plenty of time for relaxed island living.

Rurrenabaque is part of a journey through the Bolivian Amazon. After arriving, travelers pass through the town center to the river port.

From here, they travel by motorboat along the Beni River toward San Miguel del Bala. The town marks the start of the waterborne part of the itinerary, which continues with jungle walks and a visit to Madidi National Park.

## Towns Among Coffee Plantations

The Route of Flowers, or Ruta de las Flores, runs through the mountainous western part of El Salvador between Sonsonate and Ahuachapán. It connects Nahuizalco, Salcoatitán, [Juayúa](/el-salvador/place/juayua/), Apaneca and [Ataco](/el-salvador/place/concepcion-de-ataco/). Each town has its own crafts and atmosphere, while the road between them passes through green hills and coffee fields.

## Highlights Along the Way

A journey along the Route of Flowers is made up of small pleasures: strolling along town streets, discovering the work of local artisans, having lunch with Salvadoran dishes and enjoying a cup of coffee grown in the surrounding region. In Ataco, colorful murals and textile workshops add to the experience.

The region also suits a more active itinerary. Nature walks, visits to coffee farms and other activities are selected according to the route and travel time; not every local attraction is automatically included in every tour.

## The Route of Flowers on a Journey

On the [six-day tour of El Salvador](/el-salvador/tour/el-salvador-san-salvador-suchitoto-gulf-of-fonseca/), the Route of Flowers comes after the volcanic part of the second day. The following day, travelers visit Ataco. This combination reveals both the natural scenery of the coffee-growing region and everyday life in its towns.
